historical_claims.anchor: Nils Per-Åke Wedin.
The official university directory from nineteen seventy-eight places him at Umeå University
A later university record identifies him as a docent
the university's computing-science directory lists him as professor emeritus.
In nineteen sixty-nine, a technical report on pseudoinverses of perturbed matrices appeared from the Department of Computer Science at Lund University.
His nineteen seventy-two paper on singular-subspace perturbations was published in BIT, the Nordic numerical mathematics journal.
In that same period he circulated a report from Lund on the geometry of nonlinear least squares.
In nineteen seventy, Chandler Davis and William Kahan published a major treatment of the rotation of eigenspaces under perturbation.
The abstract of his nineteen seventy-two paper explicitly identifies the Davis–Kahan sine-theta theorem as a special case
Wedin's central estimate binds the two rotations together while respecting their separate spaces.
This example appears in Stewart's later survey of singular-value perturbations
George Stewart later used the memorable term ghost singular values
His original nineteen seventy-two abstract names overdetermined linear systems and rank-deficient approximations as applications.
His nineteen seventy-three papers continued directly into perturbation theory for pseudoinverses and the nearly rank-deficient least-squares problem.
Gene Golub and Victor Pereyra developed influential variable-projection methods for problems of this sort.
historical_claims.source_locator: Ruhe–Wedin 1980 abstract compares Golub–Pereyra variable projection

historical_claims.anchor: In nineteen eighty, Axel Ruhe and Wedin published *Algorithms for Separable Nonlinear Least Squares Problems* in *SIAM Review*
Wedin also worked with Per Lindström on a nineteen eighty-four line-search algorithm for nonlinear least squares.
Later collaborations at Umeå explored weighted and constrained least squares, modifications of QR decompositions, regularization, and parameter estimation in systems of differential equations.
In nineteen ninety-three Inge Söderkvist and Wedin published *Determining the Movements of the Skeleton Using Well-Configured Markers* in the *Journal of Biomechanics*
They formulated the rigid-motion fit using singular value decomposition and developed a geometrically interpretable condition number
with Mårten Gulliksson and other colleagues he published on weighted and constrained least squares
With Lennart Edsberg he worked on numerical parameter estimation for differential-equation systems
In November two thousand five, Umeå University hosted a conference on least squares and optimization in his honor.
In nineteen ninety-three Mårten Gulliksson completed a doctoral dissertation at Umeå titled *Algorithms for Overdetermined Systems of Equations*
